details: CONFIRMED that the pattern flags a description and a heredoc line (probe below); PLAUSIBLE that this is what failed at 9bc988d

True {'command': 'cat > brief.md <<EOF\nopenspec is off here\nEOF', 'description': 'Write brief'}
scan of /private/tmp/e-*/out/trace.jsonl: 692 Bash calls, keys {description, command, timeout}, 5 descriptions contain "openspec".
git merge-base --is-ancestor 5485b3c 9bc988d -> true (the failing run used the current pattern).
failing_case: The queue item names two failures: aa8cfd1 run 1 (worker-started, fixed here) and 9bc988d run 3 (no-openspec-command). The
change names no cause for the second; the fixer's report says "the other graders were right" only because it did not recur in
24 runs. The grader is applied as a JS RegExp to the whole Bash input JSON, description included, and its separator class
[;&|(] also fires inside the description or a heredoc:
{"command":"ls -la","description":"List the project (openspec folder too)"}  -> match (grader fails a correct run); should not match
{"command":"cat > brief.md <<EOF\nopenspec is off here\nEOF","description":"Write brief"}  -> match; should not match
Bash descriptions naming openspec are real: 5 of 692 kept Bash calls have one (e.g. "Read brief and list openspec folder").
fix_hint: Anchor the separators inside the command string: prefix the shell alternatives with "command":\s*"(?:[^"\\]|\\.)*? so a match
cannot start in the description (JSON.stringify keeps command first, as the traces show); or record in the item, with this
probe, that the 9bc988d cause stays unknown and add the description case as a test. Keep the three twin graders identical.
